newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends barely lower in rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends barely lower in rangebound trade.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed weaker amid mostly trade selling, as players brushed off the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly supply and demand data.
Analysts said prices had already absorbed the estimates and players were reluctant to become more aggressive on either side amid a lack of other news.
Prices held close to unchanged for most of the day, and eased to the day's lows on the close.
Volume was estimated at 22,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's official 27,220 lots, NYCE said.
The July cotton contract closed 0.26 cent lower at 73.38 cents per lb, having traded from 73.90 to 73.30 cents. New crop December went out 0.04 cent higher at 76.19 cents.

Resistance was seen at 73.50 and then at today's high of 73.90 cents in July, which is also a high reached on June 2. Firmer resistance stands at 74.10 cents, where traders expect to uncover buy stops.
In its supply and demand report issued early today, the USDA lowered China's ending stocks by 1.7 million bales from last month's estimate of 17.1 million bales.

While the reduction was lower than expected, "the real key in the longer term is whether the USDA lowers stocks again on the next report," a trader said. "Some people were looking for more, but I thought it was healthy.
